scenario: Open an app without organising anything
translation: General, no Project, launcher or Overview; window joins available tiles.
alternative_comparison: Keep this zero-setup route. Neutral for one app; potentially more overhead than a plain taskbar.

scenario: Switch rapidly among favourite apps
translation: Numbered hotbar focuses or parks its single demo window.
alternative_comparison: Stable slots and visible numbers are promising; benchmark against taskbar shortcuts before calling it faster.

scenario: Temporarily consult a calculator or dictionary
translation: Open a small window then park it; catalog Calculator is a launch toast.
alternative_comparison: An ephemeral window should leave no Project or Mode behind. Current demo is worse than a real calculator.

scenario: Keep music playing while doing other work
translation: Overview media controls share player state across Workspaces.
alternative_comparison: Good fit for a global service; a local player window need not appear everywhere. Real playback remains simulated.

scenario: Answer a message and immediately return
translation: Use a notification action or a small temporary chat window.
alternative_comparison: Inline replies would reduce disruption. Native notification/app actions are required; current demo cannot do this.

scenario: Switch an entire work context
translation: Workspace restores its Areas, active Project and windows.
alternative_comparison: Likely favourable for recurring school/work contexts; a full Workspace is excessive for every short interruption.

scenario: Find a known application by typing
translation: Super/Overview, type, choose result; browser uses fallback shortcuts.
alternative_comparison: Comparable to existing launchers. Discoverability comes from combining results rather than inventing another shortcut.

scenario: Find an unfamiliar app by category
translation: Overview offers thirteen categories and recognisable app icons.
alternative_comparison: Useful for exploration; keyboard search usually needs fewer steps once the name is known.

scenario: Recover a parked window quickly
translation: Live card and its matching hotbar number restore the window.
alternative_comparison: Potentially better than icon-only minimisation; many rich cards can make scanning slower. Offer a dense list as well.

scenario: Open an app already running
translation: Launcher focuses its existing frame; hotbar can park it.
alternative_comparison: Separate Focus from New window. Current singleton model is worse whenever the user needs another document instance.

scenario: Copy between two folders
translation: Dolphin shape is present, but no real copy and no second instance.
alternative_comparison: Keep native split view or two file windows. Project resources supplement file management; they cannot replace it.

scenario: Drag a file into another app
translation: No real file payload or receiving application exists.
alternative_comparison: Preserve normal OS drag-and-drop and a keyboard file-picker route; Areas must not intercept a file drag as a window drag.

scenario: Rename, move and organise batches of files
translation: Demonstration file rows do not implement batch operations.
alternative_comparison: Use native file manager; no advantage follows from Projects alone. Current demo is substantially less capable.

scenario: Trash and restore an accidentally deleted file
translation: Move to Trash removes a demo row; no actual trash/recovery workflow.
alternative_comparison: Real undo and Trash are essential. Removing a Project link must be distinct from deleting the source file.

scenario: Open or save a file from any application
translation: Workspace Home and Project folder are displayed, not OS dialog defaults.
alternative_comparison: Offer Current Project, Workspace Home and Recent in native dialogs; preserve access to all other folders.

scenario: Associate a video stored outside the Project
translation: Add an absolute path as a resource with its original location.
alternative_comparison: Favourable organisation without copies; existence, availability, rename tracking and launch still need a file service.

scenario: Reuse one source in several Projects
translation: Each Project can hold a reference to the same path.
alternative_comparison: Like collection membership rather than duplication. Show provenance and shared ownership; unlink must not delete.

scenario: Search a Project note or resource
translation: Overview indexes Project names, paths, Modes, resource labels and quick notes.
alternative_comparison: Favourable context retrieval; this is metadata/quick-note search, not a general filesystem index.

scenario: Find text inside a personal note or arbitrary PDF
translation: Personal Notes test phrase has no local result; real PDF contents are not indexed.
alternative_comparison: Add scoped content search and previews. Current demo is worse than a native indexed search service.

scenario: Remove a reference and keep it removed
translation: Remove link removes its DOM row, but reload restores it from saved Project data.
alternative_comparison: Persist the resource mutation and add Undo. This is a reproduced implementation bug, not a philosophical tradeoff.

scenario: Arrange reference and editor side by side
translation: Bounded split tiling fits between fixed Areas.
alternative_comparison: Likely favourable for repeated comparison; preserve minimum usable sizes and explicit split control.

scenario: Compare two documents from the same app
translation: Only one frame per app; tabs do not supply two independent OS windows.
alternative_comparison: Window-instance identity and a New window action are prerequisites. Current demo is worse than conventional desktops.

scenario: Open another app when space is tight
translation: Engine fits usable tiles or parks a peer into Apps.
alternative_comparison: Potentially better than unusably tiny tiles; worse if the reference being consulted disappears unexpectedly. Show why and allow undo.

scenario: Resize a split without moving Areas
translation: Shared divider redistributes bounded space; Areas remain fixed.
alternative_comparison: Good predictable default. Manual resizing must not silently reshuffle the user's chosen work context.

scenario: Float a small utility over the work
translation: Float context action or middle/Alt drag detaches at a sensible size.
alternative_comparison: Helpful for temporary tools; new tiles avoid it. Keyboard placement and a non-drag positioning control are still missing.

scenario: Keep a floating reference always available
translation: Floating obstacles are avoided; there is no complete explicit pin/always-on-top policy.
alternative_comparison: Add optional pin and scope, not compulsory floating. Compare a native always-on-top tool for precision.

scenario: Enlarge an app but keep Areas visible
translation: Maximise between Areas; peers park and can return.
alternative_comparison: A strong fit for alternating focus and context, subject to understandable restore behaviour.

scenario: Use actual fullscreen for game or media
translation: True fullscreen borrows Area space and parks obscured peers.
alternative_comparison: Preserve standard fullscreen expectations. Real exclusive rendering and app-specific minimisation side effects are not tested.

scenario: Manage twenty or more windows
translation: Five singleton app frames cannot represent this workload.
alternative_comparison: Use per-window cards plus grouping/filtering, optional dense views and overflow beyond nine hotbar slots. Current scalability is unproven.

scenario: Handle dialogs, tool palettes and child windows
translation: Demo editors/modals isolate background and return focus; real app window relationships are absent.
alternative_comparison: Treat a modal or transient as belonging to its parent, not a new tile or separate task. Needed for native compatibility.

scenario: Switch School to Work without losing layout
translation: Independent Area positions, windows and selected Project restore.
alternative_comparison: Likely favourable for repeated contexts. A simpler arrangement switch may be enough when folder/account defaults need not change.

scenario: Use ordinary files with no active Project
translation: General supports a normal Home and app window; Project Area can be absent.
alternative_comparison: Essential for casual use and initial learning; never require naming a Project before saving or opening a file.

scenario: Create a Project in any existing folder
translation: Project editor accepts a custom root and illustrates an editable dotfile.
alternative_comparison: Good fit; actual dotfile creation and folder permissions are native work, not implemented by the editor.

scenario: Alternate research, design and build in one Project
translation: Project Modes retain different app/window arrangements and shared resources.
alternative_comparison: Likely favourable for multi-tool phases. Do not duplicate app-internal layouts or imply modes stop background work.

scenario: Pause one Project and resume it later
translation: Close Project parks its saved session; reopen from Overview.
alternative_comparison: Promising compared with reconstructing windows; current restoration is demo state, not real documents or processes.

scenario: Work on two Projects simultaneously
translation: One active Project per Workspace; no two concurrent Project Areas.
alternative_comparison: Keep one focused Project but allow reference windows linked to another; use another Workspace only when genuine context separation is needed.

scenario: Open the same Project from another Workspace
translation: Project definition is shared; active Project/Mode is Workspace scoped.
alternative_comparison: Useful reuse; make ownership of notes, mode definitions and live window sessions explicit to avoid mistaken copies.

scenario: Keep a shared chat or music tool across contexts
translation: Music state is global, but no general user-selectable window scope exists.
alternative_comparison: Offer This Mode, This Workspace or All Workspaces. One service with several views is preferable to duplicated processes.

scenario: Reuse a virtual-desktop workflow without virtual desktops
translation: Projects/Modes can represent task arrangements; Workspaces represent broader contexts.
alternative_comparison: Translate by intent, not desktop number. Add a lightweight temporary arrangement for unrelated short tasks; new Homes for each old desktop would be worse.

scenario: Send a Project or Workspace to a colleague
translation: Pack/Import are preview dialogs, not a usable transfer pipeline.
alternative_comparison: Choose template, references or bundled files; preview missing apps, permissions and secrets. Packaging is not backup or process migration.

scenario: Read a source while taking notes
translation: School scene places reading, Project quick note and reference resources together.
alternative_comparison: Likely favourable contextual visibility; real reader/note integration still needs native apps.

scenario: Write a paper with citations and source PDFs
translation: Project links organise sources; Writer/real PDF reader do not run.
alternative_comparison: Keep Zotero and editor functionality; Projects provide a shared launch/context layer rather than another citation database.

scenario: Compare spreadsheets and prepare a report
translation: Calc is a toast; independent spreadsheet windows are absent.
alternative_comparison: Two usable document instances and internal app splits are needed. Areas should rail when the sheet needs width.

scenario: Attend a class while reading and taking notes
translation: The arrangement is expressible, but there is no call/media capture app.
alternative_comparison: Permit pinned class audio/video and a small status card; actual meeting app decides capture, mute and background behaviour.

scenario: Return to several courses with different material
translation: School Workspace plus one Project per course and Modes per activity.
alternative_comparison: Good fit if Projects are quick to open; switching context should not reset a live lecture or shared timer.

scenario: Capture an idea unrelated to the current task
translation: Personal Notes and Project quick note are separate; no automatic classification is needed.
alternative_comparison: Default quick capture to an Inbox, then explicitly attach later. Automatically saving into the active Project risks misfiling.

scenario: Review or annotate a document on a tablet
translation: Desktop shape exists but no pen/annotation workflow or hardware test.
alternative_comparison: Use a touch/pen-aware app; replace middle-button operations with visible commands and maintain undo.

scenario: Track deadlines while concentrating on one document
translation: Calendar/timer/notification widgets remain visible or accessible on a rail.
alternative_comparison: Promising peripheral awareness; a real calendar and scoped priority rules matter more than visual styling.

scenario: Prepare slides with a presenter view
translation: Fullscreen/display allocation is demonstrated, not presenter routing.
alternative_comparison: Choose audience display explicitly; keep notes private. An unused display is not necessarily safe for Areas.

scenario: Print, scan, sign and submit documents
translation: No print queue, scanner, signing or upload integration.
alternative_comparison: Retain native application/service flows. A System job widget may improve progress visibility, but cannot replace them.

scenario: Use editor, terminal, docs and preview together
translation: Work Build scene demonstrates the arrangement and shared simulated terminal handler.
alternative_comparison: Strong conceptual fit, while real compiling/debugging still needs native applications.

scenario: Use several repositories in one task
translation: One Project root plus linked resources can express references, not multi-root app semantics.
alternative_comparison: Let the editor own multi-root build/debug scope; Project may launch its workspace file. Do not equate desktop Workspace with IDE workspace.

scenario: Keep several terminal sessions and remote shells
translation: Only one Konsole frame with a simulated command parser.
alternative_comparison: Native tabs/splits or multiple sessions must preserve process identity, cwd and remote target. Current demo cannot represent real sessions.

scenario: Run a long compile or render while changing Mode
translation: Mode layouts switch, but no real background process or completion job exists.
alternative_comparison: Parking must preserve execution; publish progress/errors in a scoped live card. Layout change must not cancel a job.

scenario: Model then texture the same 3D asset
translation: Project Modes organise external apps; Blender launch is a toast.
alternative_comparison: Desktop Modes arrange tools around Blender; Blender's own workspaces control its editors. Connect these only through explicit app integration.

scenario: Edit video with timeline, preview and files
translation: Short Film modes/resources illustrate the concept, not Kdenlive operation.
alternative_comparison: Large usable canvas takes priority; rail secondary Areas and park low-priority tools. Native app minimums should guide placement.

scenario: Paint with tool palettes and a reference image
translation: No actual Krita or palettes; floating obstacle mechanism is available.
alternative_comparison: Keep palette-parent relationships and pen access; avoid parking a required reference merely to fit a new app.

scenario: Debug a browser plus local server and logs
translation: Work scene simulates terminal/preview; no browser devtools or server process.
alternative_comparison: Treat devtools as application-owned unless undocked; remember URLs and process configuration through adapters, not screenshot geometry.

scenario: Review output without altering the editing session
translation: Review Mode can retain a separate window arrangement.
alternative_comparison: Favourable if editing process/document identity persists; do not reload unsaved documents when switching arrangements.

scenario: Automate batch exports or repetitive file transforms
translation: No automation engine or file-processing integration.
alternative_comparison: Use app scripts or OS automation; expose trusted named actions and job status in Project, with permissions separate from appearance.

scenario: See an incoming notification without a second popup
translation: Expanded System Area shows inline notifications; rail/hidden state uses a discreet peek.
alternative_comparison: Potentially better attention locality; visible Area does not guarantee the person noticed it. Offer history and per-source priorities.

scenario: Mute distractions during a meeting or recording
translation: Focus/timer interaction exists; real source filtering and capture privacy are absent.
alternative_comparison: A Presentation/Focus policy should suppress previews and glow, while explicitly allowing urgent events. Current state is not sufficient.

scenario: Reply or take action from a notification
translation: Prototype notification actions are mostly dismiss; no real reply integration.
alternative_comparison: Use app-provided actions; keep original message provenance and access controls. Neutral until native integration.

scenario: Control media without restoring its window
translation: Elisa live card supports playback controls and position.
alternative_comparison: A clear potential advantage over an icon-only taskbar; compare existing OS media controls, not an artificially empty baseline.

scenario: Keep a video in picture-in-picture while reading
translation: A floating app demonstrates placement, not a real video surface.
alternative_comparison: PiP needs lightweight content, audio and controls rather than shrinking a complete app. This parallels live-card philosophy.

scenario: Share just one app instead of the whole desktop
translation: No native screen-sharing portal or real application capture.
alternative_comparison: Offer explicit Window, Display and Project sharing choices; a full-display capture can include Areas or Overview.

scenario: Record the screen or take a screenshot
translation: Catalog Spectacle/OBS entries are toasts; browser automation screenshots are external tests.
alternative_comparison: Integrate native capture with clear preview and privacy redaction; do not count a test screenshot as a product feature.

scenario: Keep a call connected while changing Workspace
translation: Window context switching works; no actual call service is present.
alternative_comparison: Default call/audio session to global service, with Workspace-local views. Otherwise context switching would unexpectedly hide essential controls.

scenario: Gather, sort and paste snippets
translation: Project/Workspace clipboard is advertised, but Copy reference does not update the clipboard.
alternative_comparison: Need real history, scope switching and an explicit transfer route; OS Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V must remain predictable. Current demo is worse.

scenario: Continue a task from phone to desktop
translation: Phone status/ping is simulated, not task transfer.
alternative_comparison: Transfer link/document/task handle rather than window pixels; surface in the matching Project or a neutral Inbox.

scenario: Game fullscreen with music/chat on another monitor
translation: Fullscreen moves Areas when spare display capacity permits; media state remains controllable.
alternative_comparison: Potentially favourable; app-specific minimisation, game capture and real compositor behaviour remain untested.

scenario: Play while downloading or updating in background
translation: No download queue or real network/process management.
alternative_comparison: Let the app own bandwidth policy; System jobs can show progress. Being parked must not imply an app is stopped.

scenario: Open a manual or guide while playing
translation: Float or second-display reference arrangement is possible.
alternative_comparison: Useful outside exclusive fullscreen; a game overlay has different capture/input constraints. Do not promise browser float is an in-game overlay.

scenario: Use a small laptop on a desk or train
translation: Engine has narrow-space tests; browser readability at those sizes is unverified.
alternative_comparison: Use rails, one useful app and quick access; make Project optional. A large default set of Areas can be worse than a simple maximised app.

scenario: Use a very wide ultrawide display
translation: Engine stress includes 3440/5120 bounds, not matching viewport visual tests.
alternative_comparison: Control tile proportions and maximum reading width; do not stretch every widget merely to fill space.

scenario: Extend across two monitors without duplicating windows
translation: Same-origin/profile second tab uses display assignment and shared state.
alternative_comparison: Model translates; real monitor discovery, scaling and independent pointer edges require native compositor integration.

scenario: Keep a fixed reference screen while switching work
translation: Workspace session is global; no user-facing independent/pinned Workspace per display.
alternative_comparison: Offer a pinned reference surface or global window scope before inventing extra virtual desktops. Current layout lacks this choice.

scenario: Undock a laptop and recover windows
translation: Closing the second test tab recovers single-display arrangement.
alternative_comparison: Preserve remembered external-display placement, offer restore on reconnect, and test physical unplug plus fractional scaling.

scenario: Use a projector that should show only the presentation
translation: Display allocation considers space, not audience/privacy roles.
alternative_comparison: Audience flag must prevent automatic Area relocation onto the projector. This is a design requirement, not just native wiring.

scenario: Use a phone/tablet with mouse, keyboard and external display
translation: Desktop has no validated touch/docked-device adaptation.
alternative_comparison: Saved app pairs and tablet windows suggest simpler layouts; every middle-drag action needs a discoverable alternative.

scenario: Launch and switch apps with keyboard only
translation: Overview keyboard navigation and Alt hotbar fallback are tested.
alternative_comparison: Good start; native Super routing and large-window lists still need work. Not a full keyboard-accessibility certification.

scenario: Move or resize a docked Area without dragging
translation: Area resize button accepts focus but ArrowLeft leaves its width unchanged; edge/reset menu is available.
alternative_comparison: Add click/keyboard size presets or numeric sizing, and directional dock commands. Existing edge/reset access is only a partial alternative.

scenario: Precisely position a floating window with keyboard
translation: Float/Grow/Shrink context actions exist; no complete coordinate/move mode is implemented.
alternative_comparison: Offer keyboard Move/Resize and click-based placement. Preserve normal tiled divider keyboard controls.

scenario: Use a trackpad with no middle mouse button
translation: Alt+drag and context Float provide alternatives.
alternative_comparison: Good conceptual fallback; teach it locally and avoid conflicts with application modifiers. Hardware path is not tested.

scenario: Use screen reader to understand changing window state
translation: Many controls have names and modals have focus handling; no real screen-reader session was performed.
alternative_comparison: Announce parking, active Project and display movement; expose ordered windows and restore focus meaningfully.

scenario: Use high zoom or large text
translation: Tiling geometry is tested, not 200/400 percent content accessibility.
alternative_comparison: Reflow Areas and Overview, allow opaque accessibility theme and stable text sizes. Never infer compliance from engine bounds.

scenario: Use high contrast or colour-vision differences
translation: Light/dark/OLED/Auto and app accents exist, without formal contrast evaluation.
alternative_comparison: Always pair tint/light with labels, shapes and state text; offer less transparency and native cursor fallback.

scenario: Reduce motion, flashing and attention effects
translation: Reduced-motion styles exist; end-to-end preference coverage is unverified.
alternative_comparison: Suppress animated background/notification trails and cursor lights while retaining static state indicators. A cosmetic motion toggle is insufficient.

scenario: Use touch, stylus or eye-gaze input
translation: Browser demo has no hardware validation; drag-heavy manipulation remains.
alternative_comparison: Larger targets, single-pointer alternatives and explicit context actions should preserve the model without relying on hover or middle click.

scenario: Use a different keyboard layout or customised shortcuts
translation: Browser fallback shortcuts work in tests; physical remapping and layouts are not validated.
alternative_comparison: Make bindings remappable, expose the actual binding and distinguish launcher slot from window number.

scenario: Keep work and personal web accounts apart
translation: Workspace content/layout changes but no distinct browser profile or cookie jar exists.
alternative_comparison: Bind app launch configuration to Workspace, with an explicit global exception. Home folders alone do not separate web identity.

scenario: Share the computer with another real person
translation: Workspaces are contexts within one user, not authenticated accounts.
alternative_comparison: Keep real OS users, guest sessions and locking. Current Workspace switching must never be presented as a security boundary.

scenario: Move a resource between Workspace Homes
translation: Locations are illustrative and mutually visible by design; no file move exists.
alternative_comparison: Copy/move/link must be explicit with provenance, overwrite/conflict handling and Undo. Context separation is organisational.

scenario: Use cloud or external-drive resources offline
translation: Stored paths remain visible; file availability or cloud download state is unknown.
alternative_comparison: Show offline/missing/moved states and reconnect actions; offer bundle or pin-offline before travel. A reference is not a local copy.

scenario: Recover after crash, reload or storage failure
translation: Notes/layout/session persistence and blocked-storage handling are tested in bounded cases.
alternative_comparison: Provide backup/migration and explicit degraded-storage notice; browser reload is not OS crash or unsaved-app recovery.

scenario: Restore a previous file version or layout
translation: No actual file version restore or user-visible general layout undo history.
alternative_comparison: Keep native file backups; add layout undo separately. Exported Project definitions do not protect every source file.

scenario: Run a trusted routine or scheduled task
translation: Terminal parser is illustrative; no real scheduler or privileged execution.
alternative_comparison: Use explicit app/OS automation hooks with permissions and job history, not an executable file hidden in a shared template.

scenario: Manage installation, permissions and device settings
translation: Discover, partitions, settings and network controls do not affect the real OS.
alternative_comparison: Keep native trusted system dialogs; System Area is a front door, not a replacement for permission/security mechanisms.

scenario: Continue long jobs through sleep and wake
translation: Short timer start/pause was tested; long expiry, suspend and real job recovery were not.
alternative_comparison: Use deadline timestamps for timers and resumable job services; background throttling must not lose completion or duplicate alerts.

scenario: Edit the extended desktop simultaneously on both screens
translation: Sequential cross-tab tests pass; one prior transient state reversal was not reproduced reliably.
alternative_comparison: Use revisioned mutations, per-object ownership and disconnect reconciliation; a broadcast snapshot is not transactional sync.
